abstract: We prove analogues of Tur\'an's theorem and the Erd\H{o}s--Stone theorem for graph $a$-numbers. The $i$th $a$-number $a_i(G)$ equals the $i$th rational Betti number of the real toric manifold associated with the graph associahedron of $G$. We show that the Tur\'an graph $T_r(n)$ maximizes every $a$-number among $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices. We also show that for any fixed graph $H$ with at least one edge and each fixed $i\geq1$, the limiting extremal density of the $i$th $a$-number among $H$-free graphs depends only on the chromatic number of $H$. Since $a_1(G)$ is the number of edges of $G$, these results recover the two classical theorems in degree one and extend them to higher $a$-numbers.
hook: Turan's theorem and the Erdos-Stone theorem carry over to graph a-numbers.
summary: The a-numbers of a graph are the Betti numbers of a related toric manifold, and the first one counts edges. The authors prove that the Turan graph maximizes every a-number among graphs with no complete subgraph of a given size, and that the asymptotic density depends only on chromatic number. This is a pure proof in extremal graph theory with no applied claim.
title: The graph $a$-Tur\'an theorem
